budget.noBudget: No budget set for this period.

settings.title: Settings
settings.preferencesLead: How amounts and dates are shown, and how the app looks.
settings.budgetLead: Your income sources, and the ceiling for the spend bar.
settings.remindersLead: Whether and when to nudge you before a charge.
settings.listsLead: Categories and payment methods across the app.
settings.securityLead: Ways to sign in, and keeping the account safe.
settings.currencyHelp: Everything converts into this currency using daily ECB rates.
settings.languageHelp: Applies to the app's text and to how amounts and dates are shown.
settings.budgetHelp: With income sources below, expected income drives the period — and this ceiling clamps it down.
settings.anchorBody: Anchor the budget period to your pay day. Set 25 and the period runs the 25th to the 24th — so a salary landing on 25 September covers 25 Sep – 24 Oct. Anchors also clamp like the recurrence engine: day 31 becomes the 28th of February.
settings.remindHelp: 0 reminds on the due date. Per-subscription overrides win over this default — while reminders are on. Switching them off silences every override too.
settings.errCurrency: Use a 3-letter currency code, like DKK or EUR.
settings.errBudget: The budget needs to be a positive number (or empty).
settings.errAnchor: Pay day anchors run from 1 to 31 — or leave it empty.
settings.errRemind: Reminders run from 0 to 60 days before a charge.

incomeSources.title: Income sources
incomeSources.description: Salaries and side gigs, each on their own schedule. Every arrival shows up in the calendar and counts towards the period's budget.
incomeSources.empty: Nothing here yet — add the first job below.
incomeSources.name: Name
incomeSources.errName: Give the income source a name.
incomeSources.errCurrency: Use a 3-letter currency code, like DKK or EUR.
incomeSources.errAmount: The amount needs to be a positive number.
incomeSources.errStart: Pick the date the income started.
incomeSources.errStartAfterNext: The start date needs to be on or before the next arrival.

managedLists.title: Categories & payment methods
managedLists.description: The starter lists, yours to shape. The order here is the order the subscription form offers.
managedLists.empty: Nothing here yet — add the first one below.
managedLists.inUse: Still used by {count, plural, one {# subscription} other {# subscriptions}} — move them to another row first.

passkey.title: Passkeys
passkey.description: Sign in with Touch ID, Windows Hello or a security key — nothing to type, nothing to phish.
passkey.name: Name
passkey.nameHelp: Only a label — the key itself never leaves your device.
passkey.empty: No passkeys yet — add one to sign in without a password.
passkey.insecure: Passkeys need a secure context — HTTPS, or http on localhost. This page is being served over plain http on a network name, so browsers will refuse to create passkeys here.
passkey.unsupported: This browser does not support WebAuthn.
passkey.cancelled: The browser cancelled the passkey prompt.
passkey.alreadyRegistered: This device already holds a passkey for this account.

twoFactor.title: Two-factor authentication
twoFactor.enabled: Enabled — sign-in asks for a code from your authenticator app.
twoFactor.disabled: Add a second step to sign-in with an authenticator app.
twoFactor.helpEnable: Checked before a secret is generated.
twoFactor.helpDisable: Turning two-factor off also forgets trusted devices.
twoFactor.helpRegenerate: Regenerating invalidates every previous backup code.
twoFactor.scan: Scan the code with your authenticator app, or type this secret in by hand:
twoFactor.saveHelp: Each works once if you lose the authenticator. They are shown again on the next step and can be regenerated, but never emailed.
twoFactor.keepSafe: Keep these somewhere safe — each signs in once if the authenticator is unavailable.
